newsitem.title: USA: Armstrong World says to proceed with Domco bid offer.
newsitem.headline: Armstrong World says to proceed with Domco bid offer.

text.p: Armstrong World Industries Inc. said Tuesday it would proceed with its plans to buy Canada's Domco Inc. for $C488 million ($354 million) despite the company's rejection of the offer.
Sommer Allibert SA, a French car parts maker that owns 69 percent of floor covering specialist Domco, said earlier Tuesday it would not tender shares in Domco after the bid.
"We question whether such a rejection can be grounded in reason," Armstrong said in a statement, noting that the rejection came less than 24 hours after the buyout offer was announced.
"We don't believe that when all of the sharholders have been heard from, that this rejection can stand. Our offer will proceed," the Lancaster, Pa.-based company continued.
Armstrong is a manufacturer and marketer of interior furnishings, including floor coverings and ceiling systems, with sales of $2.156 billion in 1996.

On Monday, Armstrong World Industries said it would offer C$23 ($16.68) per share cash to purchase all of the outstanding shares of Domco. The total value of the transaction would be $C488 million ($354 million).

Later Monday, Armstrong World Industries filed a complaint in a U.S. District Court against Sommer Allibert to prevent it from merging its floor covering business, including Domco, with Tarkett AG, which competes with Armstrong in the floor covering business. That proposed merger was announced May 28.
Armstrong World Industries stock was up $1.125 to $69.875 in midday trade on the New York Stock Exchange. Domco was down $C1.50 at $C18.50 on the Toronto exchange.
